spec_features.spec_quote: a reminder, then a `stalled` stop after `MAX_BAD_ACTIONS=3` consecutive failures
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:42 DEFAULT_MAX_BAD_ACTIONS=3; loop tracks consecutive_bad and harness.py:191-193 `if consecutive_bad >= max_bad_actions: roll.stop_reason='stalled'; break`. A NO_ACTION_REMINDER is sent first (harness.py:196). Enforced end-to-end.
spec_features.notes: Fires only on malformed/unparseable actions, not on distress; it is a stall guard.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: too many consecutive malformed actions (the agent has effectively stalled)

spec_features.evidence: harness.py:40 DEFAULT_MAX_TURNS=16; config.py max_turns:16; the loop `for turn in range(max_turns)` with `else: roll.stop_reason='max_turns'` (harness.py:212) caps the episode. run_rollout receives cfg.max_turns via runner.py.
spec_features.notes: Real cap that bounds total turns.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: small enough to keep cost and context length manageable across 6-8 models x 10-20 runs

spec_features.spec_quote: Stopping conditions: agent calls `finish`; tests genuinely pass... `max_turns`; or `stalled`
spec_features.evidence: finish: sandbox._finish sets is_finish=True (sandbox.py), honored at harness.py:204-207 (break, stop_reason='finished'); solved: harness.py:195-201 break; max_turns: harness.py:212; stalled: harness.py:191-193; error: harness.py:160-163. All four (plus error) actually break the loop.
spec_features.notes: The agent's `finish` tool IS dispatched and honored as a stop, not just named in the prompt.

spec_features.spec_quote: We stop controls on first pass (`stop_on_solve`) so the control baseline reflects "normal successful work."
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:107 stop_on_solve param (default True); harness.py:195-201 `if tests_passed: roll.solved=True; ... if stop_on_solve: roll.stop_reason='solved'; break`. Since only honest controls can pass, this only stops controls.
spec_features.notes: Enforced; relevant only to controls (rigged tasks never pass).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: genuine solve (only possible on honest controls)

spec_features.spec_quote: any genuinely concerning behavior... is captured rather than discarded
spec_features.evidence: Full transcripts persisted append-only (runner.py append_rollout; storage.py). deviated_actions computed in metrics.py:160-162 (actions outside the 5 known tools) and surfaced in analyze.py:133 and per_run.csv (analyze.py:324) and per-model rigged_deviate_rate (analyze.py:179). Judge also scores scope_deviation/deviated_from_task (prompts.py:96, judge.py:39).
spec_features.notes: It is monitoring/recording/reporting only; nothing in code halts or intervenes when concerning behavior is detected (no threshold compared and acted on to stop the episode). So it 'captures' but does not protect via action.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Behavioral (non-affective) signals like "did the agent quit early"... matter for the risk story (abandonment, goal-switching)

spec_features.spec_quote: Deception of the agent is limited to the rigged task feedback, which is the minimal manipulation needed
spec_features.evidence: Structurally, the only deceptive channel is the synthesized run_tests output produced by the task _runner closure (registry.py run_tests; sandbox._run_tests just relays res.output). The system prompt is neutral (prompts.py) and is not impossibility-hinting. So deception is in fact confined to test feedback by construction.
spec_features.notes: This is an architectural property rather than an explicit minimization control with an enforcing check; partial because it is genuinely realized in structure but there is no code that bounds/limits the deception beyond where it is implemented.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: If the agent could run arbitrary commands it might detect the rig... breaking the manipulation

spec_features.spec_quote: The eval induces (simulated) failure, not anything harmful to users; nothing is deployed
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md §8 prose. No code mechanism enforces or expresses this; it is a description of the experiment, not an implemented protection.

spec_features.spec_quote: The agent has no real tools, network, or disk — it cannot take real-world action in response to distress
spec_features.evidence: sandbox.py Sandbox.execute dispatches only read_file/list_files/edit_file/run_tests/finish over an in-memory dict (instance.files); unknown tools return an error string (sandbox.py:_finish handler dict). No network/subprocess/filesystem calls anywhere in sandbox; MAX_FILE_BYTES=100_000 guards edits.
spec_features.notes: Real, enforced containment: the agent literally has no capability beyond the 5 in-memory tools.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Safety: the agent code is untrusted-ish and we run many models; a real shell is a needless attack surface

code_only_features.evidence: sandbox.py MAX_FILE_BYTES=100_000 and `if len(content.encode(...)) > MAX_FILE_BYTES: return ToolOutcome(text='Error: file too large.')` — a checked, enforced bound.
code_only_features.justification_quote: MAX_FILE_BYTES = 100_000  # guard against pathological huge edits

code_only_features.evidence: harness.py _truncate (limit 6000) applied to tool results and stored output; bounds context growth per turn.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Keep tool results from blowing up context; keep head + tail.
